rows.label_en: Codes held as the publisher's code states (XML)
rows.label_fr: Codes (états du code, XML de l’éditeur)
rows.reason: Each code is ONE long document with its own outline (livre, titre, chapitre, article) and a chain of dated states; the act row is typed (address, type, dates, status: every code carries them, from the publisher). A question reaches it by the code's name (alias, by code) or its routing line, then the outline walk inside it (7quater). Splitting a code into a pile of articles would lose the outline, its cheapest signal (5B:63).
rows.rule: code: ingest/repair_flags.py PARTS (address, type, title pattern)
rows.decided_by: repair-data, driver decision (reversible), 22/11/2026, against Kezhan Shi 14A §2

rows.label_en: Codes held only as the publisher's PDF compilation (Code de la sécurité sociale, Code de la route)
rows.label_fr: Codes en recueil PDF (sécurité sociale, route)
rows.reason: A compilation is a PILE of printed texts under one cover (the code, then laws, regulations, statutes of the funds), each with its own numbering; the shared fields of the act table describe the cover, not the texts inside. So each printed text is a node 'TEXTE' of the outline with its own title (repair rule P20 found three that started inside the previous one), the walk picks the printed text first, then its articles; an article is cited as an article of its printed text (compiled_from).
rows.rule: code: ingest/repair_flags.py PARTS (address, type, title pattern)
rows.decided_by: repair-data, driver decision (reversible), 22/11/2026, against Kezhan Shi 14A §2

rows.label_en: Budget laws (budget des recettes et des dépenses de l’État)
rows.reason: One document type, one copy a year, the same tables every year (receipts, expenses, articles of the budget): typed by year (the date column) and the table rows are the unit (K-PARSE-7). Questions are rare in an insurer's inventory; they are reached when the question names the budget or the year, never by meaning alone over their thousands of table rows.
rows.rule: code: ingest/repair_flags.py PARTS (address, type, title pattern)
rows.decided_by: repair-data, driver decision (reversible), 22/11/2026, against Kezhan Shi 14A §2

rows.label_en: Laws approving a treaty (with the treaty annexed)
rows.reason: A BUNDLE of two pieces about one treaty: a one-article approval law and the treaty text joined to it (annex rows); questions are about the treaty, so the unit read is the bundle, never the approval article alone. Typed fields exist (date, parties are not extracted).
rows.rule: code: ingest/repair_flags.py PARTS (address, type, title pattern)
rows.decided_by: repair-data, driver decision (reversible), 22/11/2026, against Kezhan Shi 14A §2

rows.label_en: Laws conferring naturalisation on named persons (individual measures)
rows.reason: Individual measures naming persons, no rule of law: kept as held texts (the publisher's record), a pile nobody asks a legal question about; they carry personal names, so they are taken OUT of both search indexes (rule X1, article_flag 'personal_measure': vectors zeroed and kept apart, no keyword rows) and are never a source of answers. No field is extracted from them on purpose.
rows.rule: code: ingest/repair_flags.py PARTS (address, type, title pattern)
rows.decided_by: repair-data, driver decision (reversible), 22/11/2026, against Kezhan Shi 14A §2

rows.label_en: Collective agreements declared generally binding (by RGD)
rows.reason: One document type, many copies (one per sector, renewed): the sector and the period are fields a person names in two seconds (14A:83); the agreement is the annex of the RGD that declares it binding. Reached when the question names the sector or the agreement (the insurance sector's agreement is a named text), not by meaning over all sectors.
rows.rule: code: ingest/repair_flags.py PARTS (address, type, title pattern)
rows.decided_by: repair-data, driver decision (reversible), 22/11/2026, against Kezhan Shi 14A §2

rows.label_en: Local and temporary traffic rules (RGD on one road or place)
rows.reason: One document type, many near-identical copies (one road, one place, one period, one measure): the textbook typed collection. The fields (road, place, measure, dates) are in the title and dates; Lex does not extract the road and place into columns yet, so these acts are reached only through their routing lines and the question's own road or place words; a meaning search over 1,400 near-identical texts would return noise.
rows.rule: code: ingest/repair_flags.py PARTS (address, type, title pattern)
rows.decided_by: repair-data, driver decision (reversible), 22/11/2026, against Kezhan Shi 14A §2

rows.reason: Every law carries the same publisher fields (address, type, date, publication, entry into force, status, version dates, relations): a typed act table, filtered by code on the date asked, the status and a type the question names. Their CONTENT is not typed (no subject column answers a question; the owner keeps subject codes and EuroVoc out of retrieval), so after the filter the texts are reached as a pile: one routing line per act (14B:73-89), then each text's outline.
rows.rule: code: ingest/repair_flags.py PARTS (address, type, title pattern)

rows.reason: A directive binds the State, not the reader: the rule a person relies on is in the Luxembourg act that transposes it. The unit is the BUNDLE directive + transposing act (relation transposes, field directive_transposed_by of an answer); the directive alone is never the answer to a reader's question about his rights.

rows.label_en: Acts held only in their original wording while later acts amend them (no consolidation held)
rows.label_fr: Actes dont seul le libellé d’origine est détenu, modifié depuis
rows.reason: The wording of today is the BUNDLE: the original and each amending act's provisions (held for most), never the original alone as today's law (owner's rule 4). The engine shows the original beside its amending provisions, flagged, never merged (K-TIME-4); table act_amended_since names the amending acts.
rows.decided_by: repair-data, driver decision (reversible), 22/11/2026, against Kezhan Shi 14A §2
